newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse touches turnover record.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse touches turnover record.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange, celebrating its 100th session on Tuesday, saw heavy trading in first-tier Azomures SA fertiliser maker ahead of its suspension on Thursday lead turnover to an all-time high.
Turnover climbed some 5.5 billion lei to 6.3 billion, the highest level since the bourse opened in November 1995. The previous record was 1.7 billion last March.
Traders and bourse officials were excited by Tuesday's performance of Azomures, which grabbed 98 percent of turnover and closed a strong 2,900 lei higher at 32,800.
"Demand for Azomures has been on the rise since January. But today several factors combined leading the stock even higher," a trader said. "What better present for the bourse?"
"Today might be the start of sustained growth ahead," said another.
Traders said buy and sell notes had been dumped into the market ahead of Azomures' suspension after a share split.
"With fears of higher inflation and a further depreciating leu and on the back of news of Azomures' privatisation, local investors bought the stock massively," said a trader.
"And we also had foreign interest in Azomures," he added.

Azomures went private last week when its main stockholder the State Ownership Fund sold 51 percent to a Romanian trader. Chunks of the company were previously sold at a public offering and through a mass privatisation scheme.
Monthly inflation is seen staying high in January, close to December's 10.3 percent, and to rise in the months ahead after fuel price hikes and expected electricity and food price rises.
"On the sellers' side, Azomures' price encouraged profit- taking," bourse general manager Stere Farmache said.
Brokers said most other prices rose due to low supply.
They said newcomer Carbochim SA, a steam generator maker, performed well, closing at 10,000 lei, seen as a good price.
"Confectionery maker Feleacul, which joined in trading also today, was not bad either," a broker said. It closed at 610 lei, compared with 1,000 at par.
Syringe maker Sanevit SA remained suspended pending an announcement on its new capital.
Two unofficial indices - the VAB and the BIG -- climbed to year highs, each rising 7.5 percent on the previous session.
Feb 11 Feb 6 Week's change 1997 high 1997 low
-- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
